recap.text: Borant burns a seasonal veto to void Celestial boxes owed to eighty-three crawlers. Quan Ch opens his box before the veto lands. He receives a level fifteen trooper in a glowing robe that lifts him off the ground.

Quan Ch flies down a train tunnel on ethereal wings and shoots blue lightning from his left hand. The front of a train crumples and the driver falls out of the cockpit. Quan Ch takes Li Jun's place on the leaderboard as a level thirty-one half-elf Imperial Security Trooper. Donut calls him a cheating poser and claims the jacket was theirs.

Miriam Dom and Prepotente stack debuffs on a boss until Quan Ch gets involved and the rhythm comes apart. Quan Ch closes in on Carl and Donut atop a spiralling aircraft, but Carl takes Emberus as his god and throws a celestial grenade. Quan Ch, level 48, reads a quest to kill a puppy and tells Tran the prize is too good. He loses his left arm and goes down a stairwell.

Quan Ch is a one-armed Crawler who specializes from Imperial Security Trooper to Sergeant-at-Arms. Princess Donut suggests Carl remove his other arm so he becomes a Sergeant. Quan Ch is no longer on the top ten and is credited with one of the fifty Odious Creepers.

Quan arrives at a church in Cuba and attempts a card battle with Imani. Invisible and missing one arm, he uses Force Plays and a hand swap to take keys from Sister Ines and Donut. A Yule Cat's Fashion Critic strips him naked before a golden Uzi Jesus shoots him and Asojano loads him with boils. Carl returns a gold ring inscribed For Daddy to Quan's hand. Quan vanishes before Carl's fist lands.

Princess Donut opens a celestial box from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions and takes out the Tiara of a Thousand Lights. She puts on Quan Ch's cloak and takes the benefits that come with it.

beats.headline: He opens his before the veto lands
beats.text: Eighty-three crawlers are owed Celestial boxes at the close of this floor. Borant appeals the ruling and loses, appeals the prizes and loses again, and then burns its one seasonal veto here, voiding the lot. It is a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch's box is already open, and you cannot un-open a Celestial box, not even with a veto. So the count comes to one: a level fifteen trooper in a glowing robe that lifts him off the ground. The veto was not mine. I want that on record.
beats.gist: Quan Ch opens a Celestial box before Borant's seasonal veto voids eighty-three prizes, summoning a floating trooper.

beats.headline: Lightning down a tunnel
beats.text: Recap, a crawler I do not usually feature: Crawler Quan Ch, flying down a train tunnel on ethereal wings, blue lightning from his left hand. The front of a train crumples and stops dead on the track, and its driver falls out of what used to be the cockpit. By the evening he has taken Li Jun's place on the leaderboard: level thirty-one, half-elf, Imperial Security Trooper. Crawler Donut calls him a cheating poser and maintains that the jacket was theirs.
beats.gist: Quan Ch flies down a train tunnel on ethereal wings and shoots blue lightning from his hand.

beats.headline: He wrecks the debuff stack
beats.text: Recap, highlights from the previous floor. Crawler Miriam Dom and Crawler Prepotente working a boss down the careful way: stack the debuffs, keep the rhythm, let the arithmetic do the killing. It is good technique and it films well. Then Crawler Quan Ch gets involved, and it comes apart. I am not going to editorialise. The footage editorialises for me.
beats.gist: Crawler Quan Ch wrecks the debuff stack while Miriam Dom and Prepotente fight a boss.

beats.headline: The plane, and the grenade
beats.text: An aircraft, spiralling down. Crawler Carl standing on its upper wing with the cat clinging to his back; Crawler Quan Ch closing in, hands glowing, to finish him. Then Carl does two things nobody had on the board: he takes Emberus as his god, and he throws a celestial grenade. The god comes to him. This file only needs to note that Quan Ch had it won, and then he did not.
beats.gist: Quan Ch closes in on Carl and a cat atop a spiralling aircraft to finish them.

beats.headline: One arm short, down the stairs
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, level 48, reads the quest to kill the puppy and tells Crawler Tran it is too good a prize, and that getting the cat would be a bonus. His robe's shield shrugs off a magic missile. A hobgoblin disco ball and a hob-lobber bring him down out of the sky. He comes back and drops Orthrus to two percent. After the grenade he attacks Crawler Carl, who is invulnerable and does not show it. He launches away without his left arm, lands by the stairwell and goes down it.
beats.gist: Level 48 Crawler Quan Ch loses his left arm and goes down the stairwell.

beats.headline: Sergeant-at-Arms
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, one-armed, pale and sick-looking on the recap, specialises from Imperial Security Trooper to Sergeant-at-Arms and keeps his place on the top ten: tenth, level forty-eight, a hundred thousand on his head. Crawler Princess Donut, watching from a personal space, objects to the plural. It should be Sergeant-at-Arm. She would like Crawler Carl to remove the other arm at their next meeting, after which he will simply be a Sergeant.
beats.gist: One-armed Quan Ch specializes as Sergeant-at-Arms, ranking tenth at level forty-eight with a hundred thousand bounty.

beats.headline: One arm, one creeper
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, one-armed, unreported all floor and long since off the top ten, has been credited with one of the fifty Odious Creepers. With two creepers still standing, the tally carries his name alongside Prepotente's ten, Louis's three and one for Lucia Mar. Crawler Carl briefly wondered whether the arm grew back. Nobody has seen him to say.
beats.gist: One-armed Crawler Quan Ch is credited with one of the fifty Odious Creepers.

beats.headline: Alone at the church door
beats.text: Location update, third phase. Subject is in Cuba, alone, with no key. He has been placed at the church, the exit for which Sister Ines holds a key, and he finds Crawler Imani there first. He attempts to initiate a card battle. She reaches the saferoom door before he can.
beats.gist: Quan is alone at a church in Cuba without a key and finds Crawler Imani.

beats.headline: Two Force Plays
beats.text: Combat log. Subject arrives invisible, from above, one level ahead of Carl and still one arm short. Peekaboo shows him Donut's hand and the nun's. A Force Play takes the Flee card sitting in Sister Ines's hand and plays it: she is out, and her key goes to the last deckmaster standing. A hand swap gives Donut three Flee cards. A second Force Play plays one. Both keys transfer to Team Quan, and he heads for an exit.
beats.gist: Quan arrives invisible and one arm short, uses Force Plays to play Flee cards, and takes keys.

beats.headline: Quan Ch is dead
beats.text: Combat log, Havana. Subject is stripped naked by a Yule Cat's Fashion Critic, shot through by a golden Uzi Jesus, blinded and loaded with boils by Asojano. He does not die at once. He asks Carl to give it back, fast. It is not the cloak. It is a gold ring from his severed arm, inscribed For Daddy. Carl drops it in his hand. She'd be ashamed of what I've become, he says. Before Carl's fist lands, he is gone. Over sixty player killer skulls.
beats.gist: A combat log in Havana shows Quan Ch is dead.

beats.headline: Donut wears his cloak
beats.text: Inventory update, ninth floor. Crawler Princess Donut opens a celestial box from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions and takes out the Tiara of a Thousand Lights. In the same sitting she puts on Quan Ch's cloak and takes the benefits that come with it. The cloak does not ask where its previous owner is, and neither do I.
beats.gist: Princess Donut takes the Tiara of a Thousand Lights from a celestial box and wears Quan Ch's cloak.
